source: 1968 English primary book; draft faithful restatements, awaiting detailed verification

problems.problem: Choose terms from the harmonic series so that the sum of the chosen terms is finite. Prove that the selected terms have density zero within the harmonic sequence $1,\frac12,\frac13,\ldots$.
Consider the iterates $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$ for $n\ge0$, with $x_0\in[0,1]$ and $f(x)=4x-4x^2$. Determine all starting points $x_0$ for which $(x_n)$ converges and find its limit.

Prove that, for every $x>0$, the infinite series $$1-\frac{1}{x(x+1)}-\frac{x-1}{2!\,x^2(2x+1)}-\frac{(x-1)(2x-1)}{3!\,x^3(3x+1)}-\frac{(x-1)(2x-1)(3x-1)}{4!\,x^4(4x+1)}-\cdots$$ converges. If $F(x)$ denotes its sum, find $\lim_{x\to0^+}F(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to\infty}F(x)$.

In a lake, $18\%$ of the fish are catfish, $2\%$ are sturgeon and $80\%$ are other fish. In a catch of $10$ fish, let $x$ denote the number of catfish and $y$ the number of sturgeon. Find the expected value of $$\frac{x}{1+y}.$$

In lawn tennis, a player wins a game upon scoring at least four points and at least two more than the opponent. A player wins a set upon winning at least six games and at least two more than the opponent. What is the minimum possible percentage of all points scored by the winner of a set?
Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial satisfying $f(0)=0$ and such that $\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ is an integer for any distinct integers $a,b$. Can such a polynomial have a coefficient that is not an integer?
Let $n>3$ be an integer. Prove that the least common multiple of all products $x_1x_2\cdots x_k$, where $k\ge1$, the $x_i$ are positive integers and $x_1+\cdots+x_k\le n$, is less than $n!$.

Let $\{m_1,m_2,\ldots\}$ be a finite or infinite set of positive integers. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the system of congruences $$x\equiv 2m_i^2\pmod{2m_i-1}\qquad(i=1,2,\ldots)$$ to have a solution.

Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, let $p$ be a prime, and let $z_1,\ldots,z_{p-1}$ be the complex $(p-1)$st roots of unity. Prove that $$f(z_1)f(z_2)\cdots f(z_{p-1})\equiv f(1)f(2)\cdots f(p-1)\pmod p.$$

For any positive integers $n,r$, prove that there exists a polynomial $f(x)$ of degree $n$ with integer coefficients such that every polynomial $g(x)$ of degree at most $n$ for which all coefficients of $f(x)-g(x)$ are integers of absolute value at most $r$ is irreducible over $\mathbb Q$.
How many nonzero terms occur in the expansion of a determinant of order $2n$ if precisely those entries $a_{ik}$ with $i-k$ divisible by $n$ are nonzero?
For which finite commutative groups is the product of all group elements equal to the identity element?

Let the line $z=\lambda$, $y=0$ rotate at a constant angular speed around the $z$-axis while its intersection point with the $z$-axis translates along that axis at constant speed. Determine a surface of revolution on which the resulting helicoidal surface can be developed isometrically; determine also the images of its axis and generators under this development.

Let a surface be covered simply by two families of geodesics such that geodesics belonging to different families meet at a constant angle. Prove that the surface is developable, that is, locally isometric to the plane.

Let $\alpha$ be a projective plane and $c$ a closed polygon in $\alpha$. Prove that $c$ divides $\alpha$ into two regions if and only if there is a straight line $g$ in $\alpha$ having an even number of intersection points with $c$.
Determine all convex polyhedra with no diagonals, meaning that every line segment joining two vertices lies on the boundary of the polyhedron.
Can three conics in the plane be chosen so that every line intersects at least two of them and through every point of the plane there pass tangents to at least two of them?
Let $G$ be a noncommutative group. Show that the set of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $G$ forms a group containing the automorphism group as a direct factor.
Choose a pairing of $2n$ distinct points on a circle uniformly at random among all pairings, and draw the corresponding $n$ chords. Find the probability that no two of these chords intersect.

A particle performs a random walk on the integer points of the real line. At time $0$ its position is an integer $x_0$ with $|x_0|\le N$, where $N>0$ is an integer. At each integer time, if its position is an integer $x$ with $|x|<N$, it moves with probability $1/2$ to each of $x-1$ and $x+1$. At an endpoint $N$ or $-N$, its next position is respectively $N-1$ or $-N+1$ with certainty. Let $P_k(t)$ be the probability that its position at time $t$ is $k$. Find $\lim_{t\to\infty}P_k(2t)$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty}P_k(2t+1)$ for each fixed integer $k$.

Place $32$ white and $32$ black chessmen on a chessboard. Two chessmen of different colours are called related if they occupy a common row or column. Find the maximum and minimum possible number of related pairs.
Show that every closed curve on the unit sphere of length less than $2\pi$ lies entirely in some closed hemisphere.
Prove that every positive integer has at least as many positive divisors of the form $3k+1$ as divisors of the form $3k-1$.
Let $t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4$ be positive real numbers, each smaller than the sum of the other three. Prove that there exists a tetrahedron whose four face areas are $t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4$, respectively.
Does there exist a Euclidean ring properly contained in the field of real numbers, but having the real numbers as its field of fractions?

Let $f$ be analytic on $|z|\le1$. For $0\le r\le1$, let $C_r$ be the image of the circle $|z|=r$ under $f$. If the maximal chord length of $C_1$ is $1$, prove that the maximal chord length of $C_r$ is at most $r$.

A point performs a random walk on a triangular lattice in the plane, moving at each step with equal probability along any of the six lattice directions. Prove that it returns to its starting point with probability $1$ if the walk is continued indefinitely.

Let $r>1$ be an integer. Prove that there exist infinitely many infinite geometric series of positive terms having sum $1$ with the following property: for every choice of positive real numbers $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ such that $S_1+\cdots+S_r=1$, the terms of the geometric series can be partitioned into $r$ infinite subseries whose respective sums are $S_1,\ldots,S_r$.

Does there exist a real-valued functional $A$ on the space of functions continuous on $[0,1]$ such that $f(x)\le g(x)$ everywhere and $f\ne g$ imply $A(f)<A(g)$? Is the answer the same if the functions are required to be monotone increasing instead of continuous?
Find all functions $f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $f(x+u,y+u)=f(x,y)+u$ and $f(xv,yv)=v f(x,y)$ for all real $x,y,u,v$.

Prove or disprove: (i) for positive integers $a<b$, among any $b$ consecutive integers there exist two whose product is divisible by $ab$; (ii) for positive integers $a<b<c$, among any $c$ consecutive integers there exist three whose product is divisible by $abc$.
Determine all finite groups that have exactly one proper maximal subgroup.

Let $R$ be a ring with identity and $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ ($n\ge2$) pairwise comaximal ideals of $R$. Prove that for any $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in R$ there exists $x\in R$ such that $x-c_k\in A_k$ for every $k=1,\ldots,n$.

Let $p$ be a connected, non-closed, simple polygonal line in the plane and $v\ne0$ a vector. Prove that if $p$ intersects its translate $p+v$, then $p$ intersects $p+v/n$ for every positive integer $n$. Does the same assertion hold for other positive real multipliers of $v$?

Given a triangle $ABC$, construct externally on its sides similar isosceles triangles $ABC_1$, $BCA_1$, $CAB_1$. Prove that the lines $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ are concurrent. Does the analogous claim hold in elliptic or hyperbolic geometry?

Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ be Lebesgue-integrable functions on $[0,1]$ satisfying $\int_0^1 f_i(x)\,dx=0$ for each $i$. Show that for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ there exists a measurable $E\subseteq[0,1]$ of measure $\alpha$ such that $\int_E f_i(x)\,dx=0$ for all $i$.
Show that a ring $R$ is commutative if $x^2-x$ belongs to the centre of $R$ for every $x\in R$.
Prove that every tetrahedron has three acute dihedral angles whose incident faces together include all four faces of the tetrahedron.

Show that a convex polyhedron with congruent faces and a vertex set of regular distribution is regular. Here regular distribution means that for any two vertices an isometry preserving the vertex set maps one to the other.
Find the minimum of $\max\{|1+z|,|1+z^2|\}$ over all complex numbers $z$.
Find the number of triangulations of a convex $n$-gon, and the number of triangulations in which each triangle has at least one side on the boundary of the original polygon.

Given $n$ points on a circle, suppose the points repel one another with forces inversely proportional to the squares of their mutual distances. Prove that the sum of the reciprocals of the distances over all unordered pairs is minimized exactly when the points form a regular $n$-gon.
Prove that a convex polyhedron has an even number of faces if every face is centrally symmetric.
